goal: backup.sh keeps a temporary working copy at a predictable path next to the source file (`<src>.backup.tmp`). An attacker who can pre-create that path as a symlink can make the script overwrite an unrelated file, and the script leaves the temporary path behind when interrupted. Fix backup.sh so it can never write through a pre-planted path at a predictable name (use a private, unpredictable temporary directory), still prints the checksum of the source's copy to stdout, and cleans up after itself.
